title: SDK keys
description: Scoped keys for the /v1 SDK API.

empty.title: No SDK keys yet
empty.description: SDK keys authorize the /v1 API for your sandboxes.

mint.title: Create an SDK key
mint.description: Pick what the key may do. Host access and CLI shells are only under Custom.
mint.usageHint: Send it as Authorization: Bearer <key> to the /v1 API.

list.allOwned: All your hosts, revisions and pools
list.otherSandboxes: May access your other sandboxes within its resource grants

revoke.title: Revoke {{name}}?
revoke.description: Requests with this key fail from now on. Work it already started is not cancelled.
revoke.typePrompt: Type the key name to confirm

form.scopesHint: Each scope must grant something on its own or with the others you pick.

mode.ALL_OWNED: All my hosts, revisions and pools
mode.ALLOWLIST: Only selected hosts, exact revisions and pools

modeHint.ALL_OWNED: Includes owned resources you add later.
modeHint.ALLOWLIST: Direct creates need host + exact revision grants; pooled creates also need the pool grant. New revisions are never granted automatically.

form.resourcesFailed: Couldn't load your hosts and templates.
form.noHosts: You have no host that can be selected.
form.noTemplates: No active revision has a verified or pending association on the selected hosts.
form.pickHostFirst: Select a host to see its revision associations.
form.poolsHint: Optional for direct placement. Pool placement also needs its pool grant, host grant and exact revision grant.

availability.PENDING: Verification pending (grantable; not ready to launch)

form.credentialsUseDisclosure: This key can put login values into sandboxes (credentials:use) and run commands or read files there. Whoever holds the key can read those values back. Grant it only to code you trust with the logins themselves.
form.loginsHint: The logins this key may use, read or change. Leave empty for none.
form.loginsRequired: With credentials:use, choose at least one login this key may use.
form.noLogins: You have no CLI logins yet.
form.ownSandboxesOnlyHint: Only sandboxes originally created with this key, including commands, files and operations. Host commands are not limited by this option.
form.hostScopeWarning: The daemon user is an Incus admin. Host commands and host file tools can reach every sandbox on the node, including other users’ sandboxes in shared pools. “Own sandboxes only” does not limit host access. Host access also requires the setting to be enabled on the node.

readOnly.title: Read-only
readOnly.description: See sandboxes, templates, pools, commands, files and operations. Changes nothing.

runSandboxes.title: Run sandboxes
runSandboxes.description: Create sandboxes, run commands in them, transfer files and destroy them.

fullAccess.title: Full access
fullAccess.description: Everything except host access and CLI shells: also templates, preview links, webhooks and CLI logins.

custom.title: Custom
custom.description: Choose each permission yourself, including host access.

sections.limitsHint: Optional: narrow what the key reaches. The defaults suit most keys.

scopeGroupHint.connect: Unjournaled interactive shell, exec and forward access to your sandboxes as the guest user. Nothing it runs or transfers is recorded, only when it connected. For CI that needs scp or rsync; leave it off otherwise.

hosts.execute: Run and queue commands on your own hosts.
hosts.files: Read and change files on your own hosts.

templates.write: Register templates, append revisions and verify host associations.
templates.build: Build template revisions from a recipe or Dockerfile, read their logs and cancel them. Creating a template by name also needs templates:write.

sandboxes.manage: Stop, reconnect, renew, rename and capture sandboxes.
sandboxes.tunnel: Expose declared ports through preview tunnels and mint access links.
sandboxes.connect: Open interactive shells and command channels in sandboxes as the guest user (not journaled).

commands.execute: Run commands, write stdin and signal processes.
commands.read: Read tracked commands; output also needs operations:read.

files.write: Write, upload, move and delete files.

operations.cancel: Cancel operations (with the scope for the work).

webhooks.write: Manage webhook endpoints that receive events for every sandbox on the account. Needs a key over all owned resources and all usable pools.

credentials.read: List login definitions, logins, accounts, instances and their events. Never returns a value.
credentials.write: Create and edit login definitions, logins, accounts and instances, pause accounts and upload values. Values are write-only.
credentials.use: Attach and free logins on sandboxes, name them at create and pin them on start. The login's value reaches the guest: with commands:execute or files:read this key can read it back. An allowlist key reaches only the logins it names.

operations.cancel: Also select the scope for the work to cancel (for example sandboxes:manage or commands:execute).

poolMode.title: Pool selection (independent of hosts/revisions)
poolMode.immutable: Keys are immutable. Losing a grant removes future pool access; regrant requires a new selected key. Retained creator work stays bound to its original create key.
poolMode.revisionContext: Pool to discover your exact revisions on foreign hosts

emptyActive.title: No active SDK keys
emptyActive.description: Your revoked keys are hidden. Choose Include revoked to see them.

useKey.title: Use this key
useKey.description: Send the key as Authorization: Bearer <key>. Keep it in a secret store or an environment variable, never in code.
useKey.curl: Check the key with curl (prints its name, scopes and expiry):
useKey.sdk: TypeScript SDK (@wssp/sdk, Node 22+). It is not on npm yet: depend on it from the wssp repository as "@wssp/sdk": "workspace:*".
useKey.cli: The wssp CLI: install it, then use the key from scripts and CI:
useKey.cliLogin: On your own computer, sign in with wssp login instead. It creates its own key.
